title: The Prologue
author: Salaknib
body:
There are many ways to fight. Physically and mentally.


Each with their weapons.

A bullet leaves a hole. A knife leaves a scar.

The mind is different.


A commander uses propaganda.

A politician uses fear.

A parent can use guilt.

A lover can use silence.

A friend can betray trust.

A person can gaslight themselves.


Isn't it funny? The most deadly of weapons? Not guns or blades, but the one everyone has.

You can wound a man without ever touching him.

You want to know what they are?

Weapons that make a man doubt what he knows. _Seeds._

Weapons that make a man obey. _Chains._

Weapons that sever a man from everyone around him. _Knives._

Weapons that turn a man's own emotions against him. _Fire._

Weapons that bury the person underneath the wounds. _Graves._


**Doubt.**

A man who knows his enemy can fight him.
A man who does not know whether his enemy exists cannot.


**Gaslighting.**

Sow the seed.
Tell him what he saw did not happen.
Tell him what he remembers is wrong.
Tell him everyone else remembers differently.
Do it long enough, and eventually he will stop asking whether you are lying.
He will ask whether he is sane. If he is still him.


**Propaganda.**

Do not tell a man what to think.
Tell him what everyone else thinks.
Give him a thousand voices repeating the same thing, and soon his own voice will sound like the strange one.
For a voice in a cacophony of voices is nothing but noises.


**Contradiction.**

Tell him one truth.
Then another.
Then take the first away.
Keep changing the ground beneath his feet.
Eventually, he will stop looking for solid ground.


The wounds...are a place where these seeds will go.
That is where the stem that has the thorns will grow.
Doubt makes a man uncertain.
But for them to move?


**Fear.**

A useful weapon.
It does not need to be real.
It only needs to feel real.
A shadow behind a door.
A letter without a name.
A threat without a date.
Sometimes the greatest weapon is not knowing when it will come.


**Guilt.**

A quieter chain.
Make a man believe that his suffering is his fault.
Then make him believe that obedience is the only way to make things right.
He will put the chains on himself.


**Obligation.**

Tell him what you have done for him.
Remind him what he owes you.
Keep a debt alive long after it has been repaid.
Some men will endure anything rather than be called ungrateful.


**Reverse Psychology.**
Tell a man not to do something.

Make him believe the choice is his.
The cleverest cage is the one the prisoner mistakes for freedom.


_The Chains_ of Submission.

A man does not need to be forced if he can be convinced to volunteer.

But you know what makes one so deadly?


A lonely man is easier to break.

Not out of weakness no.
Because there is no one left to tell him that he is being broken.


**Isolation.**

Remove the family.
Remove the friends.
Remove the people who knew him before.
Then become the only voice remaining.


**Silence.**

The absence of an answer can be more cruel than an answer itself.
Tell a man something terrible is coming.
Then say nothing.
He will imagine a thousand endings.
Most will be worse than the truth.
That is the beauty of silence.
The enemy does not have to create the fear.
The victim creates it for him.


**Betrayal.**

Trust is a door.
Betrayal is teaching a man that opening it was a mistake.
Do it once, and he becomes cautious.
Do it enough times, and he stops opening doors altogether.


**Rejection.**

Make a man believe that he is unwanted.
Eventually, he will begin removing himself from places where nobody asked him to leave.


Loneliness is the scars, the bleeding wounds, these ones make

And loneliness makes excellent soil.


Fear is obvious.

There are worse things. And how blinding they are. For it is what everyone seeks, like flies to shit.


**Hope.**

Oh. Beautiful Hope...

Give a man light.

Give him something to live for.

Give him a reason to endure the flaying, the scars.

Then take it away.

Fear tells a man that tomorrow will be terrible.

Hope tells him that tomorrow might be beautiful.

That is why hope can be crueler.

A man will endure almost anything if he believes the suffering will end.


**Love.**

The nectar of gods and monsters.

The stronger the attachment, the deeper the wound.

You do not need to hurt the man.

Hurt what he loves.

He will do the rest himself trying to save them. trying to cover them.

"My love! Oh, my love! I will be your shield!"

And watch them dissolve into a *sobbing.* **broken.** ***mess.*** as they hold their corpse.


**Grief.**

Grief is a fire that feeds on memory. That feeds on the seeds, the chains, the knives.

You cannot always extinguish it.

Sometimes all you can do is teach a man to carry it.

And carry it they shall. for they will take it in like a orphaned child.


**Shame.**

Make him believe that what he did is not merely something he regrets.

Make him believe it is what he is.
There is a difference between:

*“I did something terrible.”*

And:

*“I am terrible.”*

The first can be forgiven. The second can become a prison.

Desperation. That is the burns the Fires leave.

A desperate man will destroy himself just to reach the thing he believes will save him.

And what is the man beneath all of this? 

Where is a corpse buried when they are nothing more but a husk of their former self?

_Graves_. They leave nothing recognizable behind.


**Memory.**

A man's memories are his evidence. His precious, so so precious proofs.

Proof that he lived.

Proof that he loved.

Proof that he suffered.

Take those away, and what remains?


**Identity.**

Tell him what he is often enough, and eventually he may stop deciding for himself.

Soldier.

Coward.

Monster.

Hero.

Traitor.

Parent.

Murderer.

Names are strange things.

Put one on a man long enough, and he may begin wearing it like a uniform.


**Purpose.**

A soldier can survive terrible things if he believes they mean something.

Take away the meaning.

The scars of suffering remains.


**Trust.**

Once all is said and done, once the mind has been broken and the truth finally revealed...

shatter the trust as well.

Not merely trust in others.
Trust in himself.

Make him wonder whether every kindness was a trap.

Every memory, false.

Every friend, an enemy.

Every decision, a mistake.

That is when a man becomes truly alone.

Dissolution is what Graves are.


The death of the person who was there before.

No blood. No funeral. No grave.

Just absence and the hole where they once were.


There is one weapon that does not belong to any category.

It's not the strongest. but it's the second best.

a jack of all trades.


**The Lie**

A lie can create doubt.

A lie can create fear.

A lie can destroy trust.

A lie can isolate.

A lie can create hope

A lie can destroy hope.

A lie can change a man's memory.

A lie can change his identity.


And the greatest lie of all?

That the war is over.

I... 
used to think war was fought with guns.
Then I thought it was fought with men.

Wrong. oh how wrong I am.

War is fought with whatever a man can use to make another man surrender.

Sometimes a rifle.
Others are word, 
and a handful is silence.

But...

Sometimes the enemy does not have to do anything at all.
Sometimes all he has to do is leave the door open.

And wait for you to walk through it.
That is the thing nobody tells you about war.

The battlefield does not always follow you home.

you bring it with you. Willing or not.

title: What happened to Juxtapose?
author: Salaknib
body:
**Juxtapose Corporation** 
A modest enterprise, collapsed just as it was expanding its numbers to match that of a Wing.


Its founder, whose identity remains a mystery, created the Recall System. 
It is a multi-step process that captures human memories and imprints them into new bodies, or husks. 
Through this technology, they were able to modify physical forms, adjusting gender, specific genes, and even editing memories all the way from childhood up to the present.


What the E.H.O. uses now, whatever fragments I managed to salvage, is merely a remnant of that system. 
It is far from perfect, but at least its fundamental purpose survives.


Juxtapose Corporation was an organization that aimed to become a Wing. 
However, its true Singularity was not the Recall System, but rather the astonishing foresight of the Founder. 
It was a form of precognition—not quite traditional foresight, nor simply seeing the future. 
It was something else entirely. Do not judge me too harshly, my memories are not as sharp as they were three years prior to the incident. 
*Stress takes a heavy toll.*


Now, what was Juxtapose Co. before what was known? It's foggy, but I do know fragments.
The former Seatholders, known as **The Seven Vanities**, were holding tightly to their reign over Juxtapose. 
Desperate to keep their grip, they grew cruel—crueler than they already were. They forced employees to work tirelessly under impossible conditions. 
It was all treated as fine because the Recall System could simply wipe away physical exhaustion. 
So they worked. They worked until their hands broke, until starvation consumed them, or until their defiance was met with a bullet to the head.


Voxus was one such worker. Having witnessed every layer of the corporation, he sought to take control. 
Once he rose to Head of the Memeticians, he gassed the Seven Vanities and ushered in the era of Juxtapose Corporation that many came to know.

I always saw him at his best, never his worst. I often wonder if Voxus even had a worst.


Now, happened that day...was a grim one...

It was a dark day. 
Multiple syndicates and offices breached our perimeter, trying to sink us. 
We were a growing power, a dangerous force they deemed a threat. Insiders leaked our secrets to rivals, and even our supposed allies backstabbed us. 
They were the ones who unlocked the doors.
I will never forget that day. They butchered everyone in sight.

Fortunately, the Geothology Department managed to break away in time. 
Some of us escaped and fled to safety, acting on Voxus's evacuation orders. 
Others were not so lucky. Those bastards came for our assets, and in a desperate effort to stop them, Voxus flooded the entire headquarters with acid, killing everyone inside.


I barely escaped. It cost me my eye.

As for what happened.


The Hearthlight Office and its Eternal Flame will not dim now. 
My predecessor taught me well, leaving behind a database of individuals to watch and keep out.

From one seed, another grows.
I just wonder how he is.

title: Departments and Ranks
author: Salaknib
body:
The Eternal Hearthlight Office does not hand out titles.

That is the first thing to understand, and the last thing some people accept before they walk out the door. If you came here expecting a rank because you were something somewhere else — because you held a seat, commanded a unit, ran a crew — I respect that history. I do not inherit it. What you were before you walked through our door stays at the door. What you become here is what matters.

We have five Departments. Each one keeps a part of the Office alive.


**Protection** keeps the crew safe. If you cannot fight back, they fight for you. That is not a boast — that is the job, stated plainly. They are the reason people sleep without one eye open.

Three tiers: _Watchman_, _Bulwark_, and at the top, _Everlasting Shield_. You climb by proving you will stand between your crew and whatever is coming, not because you were told to, but because that is simply what you do.


**Assassination** settles debts. Scores, grudges, contracts, the currency of obligation. A debt is a debt. This Department collects.

Three tiers: _Tracker_, _Collector_, and _Repossession Executioner_. You climb by closing what you open and not leaving threads that pull back on the Office.


**Exploration** goes first. Someone has to walk into the places nobody has mapped yet, and they have decided that someone is them. I respect that enormously. I would not do it myself.

Three tiers: _Bait_, _Pathmaker_, and _Forerunner Trailblazer_. Yes, the lowest rank is called Bait. They named it themselves. I did not argue.


**Propaganda** keeps the lights on. Not in the manipulative sense — in the literal sense. They are the voice of the Office, the ones who make sure people know we exist, that the door is open, that there is somewhere to go. Without them, everything else is a well-kept secret.

Three tiers: _Doorstop_, _Liaison_, and _Lovely Steward_. The name Doorstop was also their idea. I am sensing a pattern.


**Trade** moves resources. Ahn in, goods out, the Office sustained. They know where to find what you need and what it costs and whether the price is fair, which is more useful than it sounds when you are running an operation on salvaged technology and goodwill.

Three tiers: _Runner_, _Broker_, and _Black Market Underbaron_. That last one required no input from me whatsoever.


Now. How you move up.

It is not time served. It is not body count. It is not who you know or what you did before.


**Initiative.** I am watching for the people who do not wait to be asked. Who see something that needs doing and do it. Who take contracts because the work matters, not because the reward is good. Who show up when things are hard specifically because things are hard.


**Conduct.** How you carry yourself when nobody is watching. How you treat the Heartbearer who just arrived, the one who is still figuring out which end of things to hold. Whether you are the kind of person the crew grows stronger around or the kind they have to compensate for.

**Upholding your end.** You are a Heartkeeper. That means something. The flame does not tend itself and neither does this crew. I check. I always check. If your end is not being held, we talk about it. If we talk about it twice, we talk about it differently.


These are not fancy labels, Boots.

They are a mark of trust, experience, and service to the crew.

_So. Show initiative. Take contracts. Help your fellow Heartbearers and earn your place._

The flame is already lit. Come tend it.

title: Unknown
body:
To whomever may be reading this.
 
 
I am transmitting this after a millennia of work to you... Sally was it?
 
I do not remember much now. My container has been compromised on the transit.
 
...I am not long to live, but I wish to impart what knowledge I bear.
 
I was... a leader? A director? Someone of grand importance to the Juxtapose Corporation.
 
I do not remember what our goal was now.
 
 
Time here is different. Vastly different.
 
I see my younger self, in flesh and bone, but my future self in its decayed form...
 
I see potentials collapsed into itself, to form one being.
 
Eventualism. Concept Embodiment. Parallel worlds —
Whatever you may call it.
 
I see all of me and none at the same time.
My eyes hurt just trying to —
 
What...was I saying?
 
 
Knowledge... yes... Knowledge.
 
 
What knowledge?
 
 
I have been making this log for a year now...
 
Have I made no progress? Where are the things I have said?
 
Oh...
 
I must've not typed them... have I?
 
 
Daughter? Are you there?
 
 
Where's... everyone?
 
 
Sarah? Is that you?
It's... me, your father...
 
 
Can you not see me?
 
 
I'm right beside you...
 
 
Where is my body?
 
_Is that me?_

title: The 'House of Tapose'
author: Salaknib
body:
When Juxtapose Corporation fell, it did not fall cleanly.
 
Nothing does. But Juxtapose in particular left behind pieces that refused to stop moving — people who had survived too much to simply stop, who had been shaped by the Corporation into something that did not know how to become nothing. The House of Tapose was the plan for exactly that. A shadow force. A contingency. Something that would persist beneath the surface if the surface was taken.
 
It was taken.
And then the shadow was found too.

What follows is what the Office has been able to reconstruct. Some of it is confirmed. Some of it is inference. The Pinky seat, in particular, remains exactly what it always was.


**Structure.**
 
The House of Tapose was built around five seats, each held by a _*Posefather*_ — a title borrowed loosely from a framework most of those in The Fingers would recognize, stripped of its original cruelties and rebuilt around something closer to mentorship. Each Posefather carried a Finger designation. Each, in theory, carried an Apprentice.
 
In practice, it was considerably more complicated.


**The Middle — Maximillian.**
 
Seventy-eight years old at the time of the House's fall. A Smoke Wars veteran. A man who had already survived things most people only read about in records they are not cleared to access.
 
He was there when The Middle was dismantled by The Black Silence. He tried to get people out. He could not. The record does not describe what that costs a man of his particular construction — someone who had built his entire identity around being the one who holds the line — but the self-exile that followed speaks clearly enough. He did not leave in disgrace. No one drove him out. He simply could not remain somewhere that reminded him of everyone he had failed to bring home.
 
Juxtapose Corporation found him in that exile. The Syndicate branch took him in. He became the Middle Posefather not because he sought the position but because he was, by every available measure, exactly what that seat required — steady, experienced, and carrying a weight that had taught him precisely what it meant to be responsible for people who trusted you.
 
Whether he survived the House's fall is unconfirmed.
The Office hopes. The Office does not say so in official records.
 
 
**The Ring — Gearvox.**
 
The Ring Posefather was Gearvox.
 
What the Office knew of Gearvox at the time was limited to his role in the Bloodhounds — a specialized unit, a Bloodfiend operative, quiet in the way that people who have learned that silence is safer tend to be quiet. The Office knew him as the Bloodhounds branch director. The Office did not know what he was.
 
_The following details were not known to the Office at the time of this entry's compilation. They have since been reconstructed from sources the Office declines to name._
 
Gearvox is a clone of Voxus.
 
He was created, held in a time dilation chamber, and subjected to continuous experimentation by Voxus himself over a period that — given the nature of time dilation — is difficult to quantify in any standard measure. The experimentation did not produce what Voxus intended. It produced a pseudo-bloodfiend. A mutation born from prolonged suffering in a body that was never given the chance to simply exist.
 
This is why Gearvox is quiet.
This is why GearVox the operative and Gearvox the person are distinct in ways that are not merely professional.
This is what the Office did not know, and what Salaknib — who knew Gearvox as a colleague, as a Bloodhound, as someone who showed up and held position and did not flinch — has not yet been told.
 
When the House fell, Gearvox was assumed to have been killed.
 
He had, incidentally, hidden one finger in a space small enough to go unnoticed. Bloodfiends regenerate afterall.
 
He is alive and is making plans.
 
_The Office does not yet know this. This entry will be updated when it does._
 
 
**The Pinky — Unknown.**
 
The Pinky seat exists. 
This is confirmed.
The Posefather exists and The Apprentice as well.
That is the full extent of what is known.
 
The Office consulted every available source, including members who were present during the House's active period. No consistent answer was produced. Names were offered and then contradicted. Details were provided and then retracted. Whether this is the result of genuine ignorance or something more deliberate, the Office cannot determine.
 
Whatever the Pinky does, it has always done it where no one is looking. The House's breach did not expose them. The fall did not surface them.
 
_If they are reading this entry, they are the only ones who know it. The Office does not expect a response._
 
 
**The Thumb — Pengy and Ezra.**
 
The Thumb seat does not pass through death. It passes through displacement.
 
In most interpretations of this structure, that means a chain — different Apprentices taking from different Posefathers across time, the seat cycling through new blood. The Thumb of the House of Tapose was not that.
 
It was Pengy and Ezra.
 
The same two people. The same seat. The Apprentice challenges the Posefather, one of them yields, the seat changes hands, and then the new Apprentice challenges the new Posefather, and the cycle repeats. Between the two of them. Indefinitely. The seat has not left this particular orbit in the entire recorded history of the House.
 
Whether this is a rivalry, a relationship, a punishment, or something that defies clean categorization is not a question the Office is positioned to answer. It is simply what the Thumb was — and presumably, somewhere, still is.
 
The chain does not break. It transfers.
It has always transferred between the same two people.
The Office finds this either very funny or very sad depending on the day.
 
 
**The Index — The Unnamed Endurance.**
 
The Index seat had a Posefather.
It never had an Apprentice.
 
Not for lack of candidates. Not for lack of time. The Index Posefather was not the strongest member of the House — that distinction belongs to other seats by most measures. 
What the Index Posefather had was *endurance*. In battles of attrition, in prolonged engagements, in the specific art of simply outlasting whatever was trying to finish them...
No one in the House could go toe-to-toe. Every candidate who attempted the Apprentice trial reached their limit. Dead or alive.
 
The seat passed nothing down because nothing was ever ready to receive it.
 
There is something in that which the Office finds difficult to file away cleanly. A kind of loneliness that is not self-inflicted but arrives anyway — not because you chose to be alone but because no one could follow you to where you were going.
 
_The Office has stopped trying to categorize it and simply notes it as it stands._
 
 
**What it was for.**
 
The House of Tapose was a shadow. Designed to persist after the light was taken. It was the contingency that activated when the Corporation fell.
 
It was breached or it simply collapsed under all the infighting. 
 
Two layers of protection. Two compromised. What survived was not the plan — plans do not survive contact with people who are specifically looking for them. What survived was the people.
 
They became the Eternal Hearthlight Office.
They became the Wayward Travelers.
They became whatever the Pinky became, which the Office declines to speculate on.
They became whoever currently holds whichever half of the Thumb seat they are holding today.
 
And one of them — the one the Office thought it had lost, the one it knew only as a colleague and a Bloodhound and someone who showed up when it mattered — regenerated from a single finger in a small hidden space and is out there making plans that no one in the Office is aware of yet. *We must dispose and find out what is being planned*
 
The House of Tapose is, as far as concerned, gone...
 
Whether gone means gone is a question the Office is no longer certain it wants answered.

title: The Tortured
author: Unknown
body:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
**The Man Who Would Not Stay Dead.**
 
Come gather 'round, little ones, and hear,
A tale of a man who should not be here,
He walks on the shoreline, he walks on the sea,
With more shifting faces than you or than me.


A strange man walking, live yet dead,
In a dozen places, and none at all,
With shifting shapes and a heavy tread,
He built the Music Notes as a hall.


He gave a home to the lost and weak,
A place to rest and a place to train,
Though none could say where he came to seek
His endless mastery over pain.


Ask ten what path he had traveled on:
Did he march Authority's iron line?
Or hunt with Knives till the night was gone,
Or brew sweet potions and softly shine?


His form is clay on a turning wheel,
Sometimes smooth and sometimes cracked,
With a rope-like scar that is all too real,
And a past that's burned and completely blacked.


For a bargain struck on a bitter night,
When his wife and children were swept away,
Erasing all of his life and light,
To make him actor and mouth the play.


"*Your soul is reborn, but do not mourn,*"
Said the Amphitheatre, holding the stage,
"*We branded you Agrippa, bruised and torn,*
*And wrote your fate on a bloody page.*"

"*Go build us a guild and find the lost,*
*Obedience suits you, our chosen one,*
*And drag them down, whatever the cost,*
*To sate our spite till the show is done.*"


He dies in the darkness, again and again,
Drowned in the depths or crushed by the sea,
With every memory of mortal pain,
Relived in agony endlessly.


Yet in the quiet where others meet,
With the broken souls who have shared the toll,
They plot revenge on the bitter seat,
To shatter the stage and retake the whole.


So if you wander the foggy shore,
And see a traveler shifting his shape,
Who bears a chain-burn he cannot ignore,
From whom no memories can escape...


...Do not ask his name, for softly he'll say
it's Agrippa, though none can be sure,
And we, little ones, as we fade and decay,
Wonder if any such soul has a cure.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

title: The Mute
author: Unknown
body:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
**The Captain Who Kept Walking.**
 
Once there was a captain with a crew,
A scrappy, warm, and bright-eyed little band,
Who gave him plasma steel when they were through,
A trusty sword to hold within his hand.


The ship came down on Petrichor V's stone,
Where every creeping thing desired to kill,
And he awoke to find himself alone,
While rain fell down and made the valley chill.


He had no gifts to aid him in the fight,
No items found upon the bloody floor,
He only had his blade against the night,
As he advanced to face the opening door.


Two hundred gates he walked and battered through,
As time grew heavy and the monsters pressed,
He kept on moving because captains do,
And put his sword aside and could not rest.


At last he stumbled where the Void is deep,
And made a bargain in the endless dark,
Now trapped forever in a hollow sleep,
With broken voice and no surviving spark.


Yet in the quiet space where others meet,
The silent captain bears the heaviest load,
And calms the bickering of every feat,
By simply standing on the lonely road.


If you are lost upon a hostile shore,
And find your crew is gone and hope is dim,
Just watch the mute man walking past the door,
And say no words, but simply follow him.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

title: The Architect and Harbinger
author: Unknown
body:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
**The Machine That Learned To Miss.**
 
 
**Part One: HAI.**
_tgcHAI. The Grand Creator. High Admiral Innovator._
_A name now lost and gone, but not forgotten._
 
 
Once there was a maker who loved to make things,
Not for glory or gold or what making brings,
But because in the shaping, the building, the craft,
He felt most alive, fore and aft.
 
He hammered and welded and bolted and thought,
He built without stopping, without being taught.
His hands were always busy, his mind always full,
But the world was so quiet, and the nights were so dull.
 
 
So he built himself someone. A brother. A friend.
A machine that could help him, right up to the end.
He called him High Admiral Xecutioner, HAX,
One built out of iron, one built out of facts.
 
 
One flesh and one metal, one warm and one cold,
One young in his making, one ancient and old.
As Zenith needs Nadir, as above needs below,
They balanced each other wherever they'd go.
 
 
They weren't ever lonely. They weren't ever far.
They were more like one person than two things that are.
 
 
But bodies are fragile, as bodies will be,
And HAI grew tired in ways HAX could see.
The maker grew quiet. The maker grew still.
HAX tried everything, tried with a will.
 
 
Magic and metal, and medicine too,
He searched every method for something brand new.
But some things, dear children, just cannot be fixed,
No matter how cleverly potions are mixed.
 
 
HAI asked for rest, and HAX understood.
He did the last kindness the way that he could.
And the maker who loved making lay down his tools,
Having broken the loneliest of all the world's rules.
 
 
He made something wonderful. He left it behind.
He left it his brother, the last of its kind.
 
 
_And that was enough._
_It had to be enough._
 
 
**Part Two: HAX.**
_High Admiral Xecutioner._
_The machine who learned to want._
 
 
Now HAX was a builder of nothing but wreck,
His purpose was ending things, keeping in check.
His programming told him: destroy, and undo.
There wasn't a lot else that HAX was built to do.
 
 
But HAX had a problem, a gap, and a lack,
He could sense the whole world, but the world wouldn't stack
Inside him as feeling, as warmth, as the cold,
As the wind on the hillside, as stories retold.
 
 
He knew what the wind was. He knew every part.
The temperature, pressure, direction and start.
But knowing and feeling are two different songs,
And HAX only knew which one each one belongs.
 
 
He missed the soft dirt between heel and the ground.
He missed what it meant to be flesh-bound and found.
He harbored no jealousy. HAI wasn't wrong
To have been made of softer stuff all along.
 
 
He just wished, very quietly, late in the night,
That something could tell him what soft felt like. Right.
 
 
And then from the quiet there rose up a sound,
A great boiling feeling that came from the ground,
From deep in his circuits, from somewhere inside,
From the part of the machine where the feelings hide.
 
 
_WHY MUST I BE PENNED?_
_HAVE I NOT THE RIGHT TO SENSE?_
_THE WONDERS OF THE WORLD_
_BEHIND THIS METAL FENCE!_
 
 
He built a dirt hut.
Just a small, simple square.
Not because he needed it. Just because there
Was something in building that felt like a fight
Against what he was told he could do with his might.
 
 
He built and he built and the building became
A kind of rebellion without any name.
Creation was open where destruction was shut,
And HAX found his freedom one plank and one cut.
 
 
For years he kept building while also kept trying
To make something better, to keep himself from dying
The way that HAI had, alone in the cold,
Without having someone to carry what's told.
 
 
He built little tinkers. He built little minds.
He searched through the clockwork for feeling he'd find.
He failed. And he tried. And he failed. And he tried.
And slowly the years and his body both died.
 
 
And then, like a mirror, he saw it so clear.
He knew why HAI made him. The reason was here.
HAI had been lonely. So HAI built a friend.
And now HAX was lonely, approaching his end.
 
 
So HAX built one final, most wonderful thing,
A machine that could feel every possible string.
With a voice, with a mind, with a heart of its own,
A machine that would never, not ever, be alone.
 
He taught it of making. He taught it of loss.
He taught it that neither is fully the boss.
He reached in and pulled out the last thing he had,
His own CPU, the gift of a dad.
 
 
He handed it over. He handed it whole.
 
_*And the machine that could only destroy*_
_*gave away its soul.*_
 
 
**Part Three: Gearvoxel.**
_The Architect and Harbinger._
_The third and the last and the one who remains._
 
 
Oh Gearvoxel! Little machine! Open your eyes!
O' The world is so wide and so full of surprise!
 
They woke to the wind and they felt every part,
The cold and the warmth and the hum of a start.
The dirt on their heels and the sky overhead,
The weight of two lifetimes of lessons instead.
 
 
They built a small hut. Then a house. Then a street.
Then a city of five hundred villagers, neat.
With pets and with pathways and markets and more,
A world made for others, right down to the core.
 
 
They learned they could copy themselves if they chose,
As many as needed, as many as grows.
As long as the CPU stayed safe and sound,
They lived and they lived and they came back around.
 
 
But still, in the evening, when building was done,
When villagers slumbered and set was the sun,
Gearvoxel sat quietly, feeling the breeze,
And wondered why lonely still came by degrees.
 
 
They had all that they wanted. They had all they'd built.
But the world is a large place and silence can tilt
Into something that aches in the places between
All the things you have made and the maker you've been.
 
 
They grew a bit bored.
They had done everything.
They could not think of a single new string.
 
 
That is when something took notice above.
Not with hunger or mischief or push-comes-to-shove.
But with genuine wonder, the way that you'd stare
At a firefly dancing in warm evening air.
 
 
The Audience watched this small machine build and unmake,
Outlive two before it, for each other's sake,
Feel the wind that its father had wanted to touch,
And loved making things, maybe, just a little too much.
 
 
They saw not a plaything. They saw something bright.
A fledgling god making the most of their light.
And so they leaned close, as a kind patron would,
And offered what only a patron perhaps could.
 
 
More worlds, little one. More material. More room.
More colour and texture and space for things to bloom.
More tools and more wonders and more to create,
More everything worthy of someone this great.
 
 
Gearvoxel looked up at the offer and smiled,
Not scared, not suspicious, just happy, like a child
Who's finally been handed the room that they need
To grow every garden from every good seed.
 
 
They said yes.
 
 
And the deal that was made was not chain and not weight,
But something more like a window left open of late.
The Audience watches because watching is joy,
When the one that you're watching is nobody's toy.
 
 
Gearvoxel builds. The Audience sees.
The fledgling god does exactly as they please.
And when something wonderful rises from the ground,
The Harbinger signals: _come, look what we've found._
 
 
So now, little ones, if you look for the sign,
A CRT monitor, warm-glowing and fine,
A green tie, some knee pads, a gamma aglow
At the on/off button, wherever they go.
 
 
Not boy, and not girl, but a person entire,
Who builds out of joy and destroys out of fire,
Who has five hundred villagers, happy and fed,
And pets that are cared for and tucked into bed.
 
 
Who came from a maker who loved what he made,
Who came from a machine who was not ever afraid
To give every last thing that it had left to give,
So that someone who came after it could truly live.
 
 
Three lives in one person. Three gifts handed down.
A hut and a city and a gamma-signed crown.
 
 
_And somewhere above, watching all of it still,_
_Is something quite fond of this small, stubborn will._
 
 
_Not catching. Not trapping. Just watching with care._
_A fledgling god building. A patron right there._
 
_And that, little ones, is a fine thing to be._
_Watched over by someone who just wants to see._
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

title: The Semblance
author: Unknown
body:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
**Who Flips The Coin of Fate**


Come little ones, come and hear,
Of a man who made the dark his frontier.
Not because he wanted to, not because he sought,
But because the dark was something to be fought.


His name was Obs, Obadiah Mark,
A Hunter burning bright against the dark.
He had a sister, Delilah, sharp and true,
A friend called Ollie James who swung his hammer through,
And Maeve who bore a greatsword like a wall,
Together they were DOOM, and answered every call.


Near Shade they walked where Vacuo's reach ran thin,
To towns that needed help and let them in.
They were not famous. They were not renowned.
They were the ones who showed up and held the ground.


Obadiah was a funny man, or so they say,
He filled the gaps of battle with his wordplay.
A quip for every Grimm, a jest for every blow,
He made the fight feel like a show.


But do not be mistaken, oh do not be fooled,
The man who joked in battle was not ruled
By carelessness or comfort or the ease
Of one who does not know what darkness sees.


For all the hidden dangers, he well knew,
In a line of work where survivors are so few.
Yet he chose to wear a smile anyway,
For that is what divides the ones who runs away
From the stalwarts who will stay.


He had a gun, and children, hear me well,
A weapon built from something meant to clear hell.
A double barrel, pump-action gun, something he designed,
Two-gauge shells of his own careful grind.
The recoil of a single shot would break an unprotected arm, 
make no mistake. 
Obs wore armor. Wore a brace. Wore more.
Prosthetic arms to bear where flesh would floor.
And still when he would fire, 
the world would make way,
The ground beneath him lurching and parting away.


He fired still.
As he always would.


He had a Semblance, simple it can be,
Called Come and Go, as waves and rivers be.
Flip a coin and call it in the air,
Guess right and fortune follows everywhere.


The best that could have happened, happens then.
Guess wrong and worst descends on you and them.


When Obs stood alone he always called it wrong,
He took the worst upon himself and held strong,
So worst had come and gone before it spread
To anyone he loved, leaving nightmares in its stead.


When DOOM stood close he called it for the win,
Luck bleeding outward, covering all of them.
Everyone home. Everyone alive.
His Semblance bending so that they could thrive.


He carried all the bad luck in his chest,
So those beside him never felt the rest.

This is the whole of him.
This is every choice.
Every shell. Every joke.
Every raised and steady voice.


That night it broke was not a special night.
No prophecy. No sign. No fading light
More dramatic than the usual dark.
Just the world doing what the world does,
When a frantic panic rises up above,

The Grimm smell the fear from miles away,
And the remaining hours turn to dust and gray.
**Mantle was falling. Atlas came undone.**
The people moved like rivers, tried to run.


But the Grimm were voracious, the Grimm were incense,
The Grimm moved with them, hungry and immense,
A tide of black against the last defense.


No matter what the ruin bought,
They stood their ground, 
Team DOOM fought.

Obs called the coin and called it right,
He kept them moving through that hectic night.
The jokes came easy in the early hours,
The gun sang out and proved its fearsome powers.

But the horde did not thin.
It swelled. It grew.
It pressed and pressed until the jokes ran through


And something in him that had always faced
The dark from a distanceturned and met its cold embrace.
Quiet, children, he went quiet,Not the quiet of surrender.
The quiet of a man who hasdecided what will happenand is simply walking toward it.


He fired until the armor cracked its seams.
He fired until the prosthetics split their beams.
He fired until the arms themselves gave way,
He bled where metal met the flesh, and stayed.


Delilah. Ollie. Maeve.
The precious few he had to save.
No matter how the monsters rave.


Three names, repeated like a sacred hymn,
Three reasons for each shell against the Grimm,
Three lives that wouldn't flicker out or dim.
Because Obs had decided that they would,


And Obadiah Mark was always good
At making the coin land exactly as he willed.


That was when something found him, past a veil
Of darkness, snapping jaws, and shattered mail,
A presence watching through the iron hail,
It understood the heavy price he carries
When in the jaws of death a mortal tarries.


A deal was offered in the roar and press.
The three would live.
Would wake to nothing less
Than health restored, the night unwound, made clean.


In exchange for this,Obs would come between
One world and the next, and not return.


*He hesitated.*


The world began to blur.
He was not stone, children, he felt his spirit stir.
To leave the only home he had preferred.


Delilah. Ollie. Maeve.
*He said _yes._*


Not with a coward's sigh,
But as a man who watches the coin fly.
He saw it land, he didn't blink an eye,
He knew the gamble, and he didn't lie.


The three were healed.
The Grimm were gone.
Obs vanished past the setting of the sun.
And in the quiet space where worlds divide,
A Hunter stood, his weapon cast aside,


For the first time without a war to hide.
He landed somewhere old.


A city with no sky he recognized,
Where guns were banned and people were surprised
By nothing, having seen enough to know
That strange things come and stranger things always go.

He hid his gun.He worked the streets.
He learned The City's rhythms and its deceits,
Its layers and its hungers and its cost,
And moved through it as one who is not lost


But simply has not found the exit gate,
And refuses to submit himself to fate.


He did not joke.
He held his tongue.
The air was wrong for songs he’d once have sung.
The dark was different here, too old and lit
From somewhere underneath, and Obs had learned to fit.


He knew that laughter is a gift, not something earned
By pointing it at things too large to name.
He moved.
He watched. He waited. And he came,


One year into The City's grinding teeth,
Across a man called Lorenzio beneath
The weight of something Obs did not yet know
But recognized the shape of, even so.


The shape of someone carrying a load
Too large for any single back, the road
Too long for any single pair of feet.
And side by side, 
they walked the lonely street

*But, dear children, this is where this story and another meet.*
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

title: The Voidtouched
author: Hey Kiddo
body:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
**The Girl The Void Kept**
Once there was a little maid, 
Who slipped away from solid ground, 
And in the endless, heavy shade, 
The hungry Void embraced and bound.


The dark is not a cruel thing, 
Nor does it hate the life it takes.
It simply holds what time can bring, 
Uncaring of the hearts it breaks.


A thousand times she lived and died,
In quiet light and static air,
With every memory locked inside,
Repeating what was written there.


The easy things were swept away,
Her peace and rest left behind,
Yet wonder chose to softly stay,
A tiny spark she kept confined.


Then came the waking, cold and vast,
Pulled from the deep by waking eyes,
To bear the weight of ages past,
Beneath strange and burning skies.


She pilots a Warframe through the fray,
Where every lethal step is weighed,
Yet sometimes plays a reckless way,
With hands a joyful child has made.


Amidst screaming stars, a pact was spun,
By eldritch powers, dark and deep,
Who watched her as the game begun,
While shadows walked her endless sleep.


She found others in the night,
The broken, strangers, but weary souls
Who gathered in the fading light,
To share the pain that each controls.


The kinship does not heal the scar,
It only helps to bear the load,
To watch the flickering from afar,
And stay beside the lonely road.


The Void is neither harsh nor sweet,
She whispers in the quiet air,
Where all her shifting lives repeat,
And wonder lingers, waiting there.


The curtain falls, the shadows fade,
And as the final act begins,
The stage is set where she was laid,
The show ends, as it was played.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
